turns.thought:
Yes — definitely turn mobile data on. MMS (picture messaging) requires an active mobile data connection, so with data disabled, photos will never send even though regular texts go through.

Here's what to do, in order:

**1. Turn mobile data ON**
- iPhone: Settings → Cellular → Cellular Data → ON
- Android: Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile network → Mobile data → ON

**2. Switch off 2G — this is important**
You mentioned you're on 2G with one bar. 2G networks generally can't support MMS at all, so even with data on, picture messages will likely still fail. Change your preferred network mode:
- iPhone: Settings → Cellular → Cellular Data Options → Voice & Data → select **5G Auto** or **LTE**
- Android: Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile network → Preferred network mode → select **5G/LTE preferred** (or "4G/5G preferred")

**3. Restart your phone**
This lets the new network mode and roaming settings take effect, and gives the phone a fresh chance to connect to a nearby tower.

**On the one bar of signal:** that's a "Poor" signal strength, which can also prevent MMS from completing even when everything else is configured correctly. After the restart, check whether the signal improves. If you're still at one bar:
- Try moving to a different spot, ideally near a window or outdoors — buildings can block roaming partner networks.
- If you have access to Wi-Fi, connecting to it will help general internet use, though MMS itself still needs to go over your cellular data.

Once you've done steps 1–3, try sending a photo again and let me know what your status bar shows — specifically the signal bars and whether it now reads 4G/LTE/5G. If it's still failing, we'll look at your APN settings (particularly the MMSC URL), Wi-Fi Calling, and your messaging app's permissions, which are the next most common causes.

Here are the steps for your records — full A to Z, including the account-side fix I made:

**Fixing MMS (picture messaging) failures**

1. **Identify the line** — confirm the account and the specific line the messaging issue is on.
2. **Check line status** — a suspended line has no service at all. If suspended due to an overdue bill, pay it, then the suspension can be lifted. (Your line was active, so this wasn't a factor.)
3. **Check roaming (when abroad)** — MMS needs mobile data, and abroad that requires the line to be roaming-enabled on the account side. I enabled this for line 555-123-2002.
4. **Turn on Data Roaming** on the device — Settings → Cellular/Mobile Network → Data Roaming. This is separate from the account-side setting.
5. **Turn mobile data ON** — MMS cannot send with data disabled, even though plain texts will still go through.
6. **Change off 2G** — 2G can't support MMS. Set the preferred network mode to 5G Auto / LTE, or "4G/5G preferred" on Android.
7. **Restart the phone** — lets the network mode and roaming changes take effect.
8. **Check signal strength** — one bar ("Poor") can block MMS even with everything else correct. Move near a window or outdoors if needed.

**If it still fails after step 8**, the next things to check are the APN settings (specifically that the MMSC URL is set — resetting APN to default and restarting fixes this), Wi-Fi Calling being ON, and whether the messaging app has storage and SMS permissions granted.

One note on delivery: I don't have a way to email or text documents out, so I've shared the steps above in this chat — you can screenshot or copy them from here.

Sounds good on the data — you've got room to spare in this cycle, and I'm glad to top you up if you start running low. Take care and enjoy the rest of your trip!
